subject: Pricing exception request — AtlasBank strategic VPC commitment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exception request — AtlasBank strategic VPC commitment

Team,

AtlasBank (large US retail bank) is requesting a commercial exception for an enterprise VPC deployment tied to a 3-year minimum committed spend. Quick context: this is a 3-year, multi-region VPC with customer-managed VPC peering, strict data residency in us-east/us-west, and a requirement for a 99.95% uptime SLA and extended audit log retention. They are a strategic reference for our banking vertical and have asked for a pricing floor that would materially reduce unit revenue.

Why I think we should approve (brief):
- Strategic value: potential reference and co-marketing; pilot with 2 business units across Q4.
- Scale: projected committed spend $1.8M ARR (year 1 annualized) with escalation to $2.6M ARR by year 3 under current usage forecast.
- Competitive risk: they are evaluating two other vendors who have offered deeper discounts tied to multiyear commits.

Request: approval for a blended discount structure that includes an upfront implementation credit and a multi-year committed discount. I attach the current SOW draft and a pricing model showing revenue impact and payback. Specific ask: sign-off from Finance (Marissa) + Revenue Ops (Marcus) on the proposed blended credit so I can present to AtlasBank procurement tomorrow.

Attachments: AtlasBank_SOW_draft_v3.pdf (SOW stub), pricing_model.xlsx (pricing workbook)

Key negotiation points to note for the memo:
- Implementation credit (one-time) vs. recurring percentage off list
- Commitment term to enforce minimum ARR and early-termination clawback
- SLO and escalation path to be included in SOW; Legal will need to confirm indemnities

Quick ask: can Marissa and Marcus review and mark whether CFO sign-off is needed or if VP-level approval (Marissa) suffices? I can prepare a short executive memo if you want it tailored to CFO language.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
M: (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exception request — AtlasBank strategic VPC commitment

Rachel —

Thanks for the concise summary and the attachments. A few items I need before I can greenlight anything:

1) Gross margin impact — please confirm net-of-cost margins for years 1–3 under the proposed structure (include expected GPU/infra costs, support overlay).
2) CAC / payback rationale — is the implementation credit being used as a sales incentive or as a true project cost?
3) Contractual protections — we will require a clear early-termination clawback tied to unpaid committed spend; Legal must sign off on indemnity and data residency clauses.
4) Forecast reliability — who owns the usage forecast? If Atlas can undercommit, we need a minimum monthly consumption threshold or utilization-based true-up.

If you can get me a 1-page executive memo addressing the four bullets and a recommendation (approve / approve with modifications / deny), I will review and aim to respond same day. Also loop in Legal if they have any immediate redlines.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Chief Financial Officer | Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exception request — AtlasBank strategic VPC commitment

Marissa —

Appended below is a 1-page exec memo and the quantitative backup (pricing_model.xlsx tabbed). Summary recommendation: approve a blended structure with a one-time implementation credit of $120,000 and a blended recurring discount that phases: ~25% (year 1), 18% (year 2), 12% (year 3) off list for the VPC SKU. That results in an average blended discount of ~18.5% over three years and preserves acceptable margins per the attached model.

One-page exec memo (for CFO):
- Deal: AtlasBank — 3-year VPC commitment; target start: Sep 2026
- Commercial ask: up to 25% discount in year 1 + $120k onboarding credit to offset migration costs
- Revenue impact: $1.8M ARR year 1 (post-discount), $2.1M ARR year 2, $2.6M ARR year 3 (projected)
- Margin impact: normalized gross margin remains above 45% net-of-infra and support (see pricing_model.xlsx, tab: margin_assumptions)
- Recommended approval: CFO sign-off required for one-time credit > $100k. Approve with condition that Legal adds an early-termination clawback proportional to remaining committed value and a utilization true-up every quarter.

Operational asks:
- RevOps (Marcus) to prepare an SOW variant with the clawback language and an enforced minimum monthly consumption threshold.
- Legal to confirm indemnity/data-residency wording; Atlas requested HSM KMS integration (we can support).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HD-987654 (pipeline notes and financial model live in the deal record).

Attachments in this message: pricing_model.xlsx (tabbed), AtlasBank_SOW_draft_v3.pdf (SOW stub)

If you approve, I propose the following communication plan to Atlas: present the blended structure and the clawback terms, offer to put implementation credit on the first invoice contingent on DocuSign execution. They need final numbers by end of week — procurement wants to show the CFO.

Thanks,
Rachel

Rachel —

I reviewed the memo and the pricing workbook. I will approve an exception on the following conditions:

1) Approved commercial structure: one-time implementation credit of $120,000 + blended recurring discounts that result in a 22.5% blended discount over three years (slightly lower than requested).
2) Contract conditions: Legal to add an early-termination clawback that recoups the pro-rated remaining committed value, and a quarterly utilization true-up.
3) Operational gating: RevOps (Marcus) to prepare the final SOW with the clawback language and the minimum monthly usage threshold; RevOps to confirm margin-neutral billing cadence.
4) Escalation/visibility: I want VP Sales to confirm we will get a reference program commitment and a public case study clause in year 2 (opt-out allowed only if Atlas breaches data residency terms).

Next steps: Marcus, please create the SOW variant and update the HubSpot deal with the CFO-approved terms. Rachel, present the approved structure to Atlas procurement (loop Elena and Daniel) with the attached DocuSign envelope for signature. Legal should be on standby to clear redlines.

Signing off conditionally so you can proceed with procurement — final DocuSign execution required for credits to apply.

—Marissa
